1:3.sourceText: Χάριν ἔχω τῷ Θεῷ, ᾧ λατρεύω ἀπὸ προγόνων ἐν καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει, ὡς ἀδιάλειπτον ἔχω τὴν περὶ σοῦ μνείαν ἐν ταῖς δεήσεσίν μου νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας,
1:3.targetText: I am thankful to God, whom I serve from progenitors in a pure conscience, that I unceasingly have remembrance concerning you in my supplications night and day,

groups.note: The thanks-have idiom χάριν ἔχω means I am thankful; both actual idiom constituents jointly support the English thanksgiving phrase.

The Greek ὡς introduces how/as the remembrance is continual; LSV uses that to connect the thankful statement with its remembrance explanation. This contextual connective rendering does not make that the general meaning of ὡς.

1:12.sourceText: δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν καὶ ταῦτα πάσχω, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐπαισχύνομαι, οἶδα γὰρ ᾧ πεπίστευκα, καὶ πέπεισμαι ὅτι δυνατός ἐστιν τὴν παραθήκην μου φυλάξαι εἰς ἐκείνην τὴν ἡμέραν.
1:12.targetText: for which cause these things I also suffer, but I am not ashamed, for I have known in whom I have believed, and have been persuaded that He is able to guard that which I have committed to Him—to that day.

groups.note: The actual Greek noun phrase is my deposit/that entrusted to me or by me, τὴν παραθήκην μου. LSV interprets this as what I have committed, converting the possessive deposit expression into a relative verbal clause. This preserves that complete actual deposit phrase without asserting that the genitive μου alone is a nominative I or resolving the deposit interpretation for every translation.
